correctness.rationale: The conditioning risk is exact. For eta=1/2 Cauchy-Schwarz excludes t<=3/4 and two exact rational lower bounds for -2(t^(3/2)+1/2)c_second bound the derivative S_prime strictly below zero for t>=3/4; S(1)=0 proves unique endpoint optimality. The endpoint comparison increases strictly with eta because c(t)<c(1). For eta<1/2 the endpoint directional derivative is negative and an interior maximizer exists by continuity. Singular t=0 and eta=0 are handled by the information limit. Symbolic, exact rational and numerical covariance checks were replayed successfully; finite tests are only supplementary.

The 2023 one-point design has a different objective (the time integral of causal state-prediction MSE, with noiseless data), not the posterior MSE of the scalar area. The related historical Volterra finding uses a nonstationary-increment prior. No retrieved claim implies the sharp global endpoint cutoff for the stated model. Earlier equivalence remains possible.

value.rationale: A fixed single-sensor budget for the time integral of a long-memory stochastic process is a natural numerical-integration/information-design problem. The theorem determines an exact sharp parameter threshold for when it becomes optimal to sample at the terminal time, a qualitative regime absent from ordinary Brownian sampling. The threshold has an analytic global certificate, not just a local stationarity test; it supplies a reproducible benchmark for resource allocation under persistent temporal correlation. The lack of a below-threshold uniqueness proof is stated, rather than silently broadened.
